intro: This week: work — a phone call with an employer, a job interview, an application by e-mail. One of the most frequent topics in the B1 exam.
speaking.0.promptUa: Describe the illustration. Say where these people are, what they are doing and how they feel. Also say what you think will happen next.
speaking.0.phrases.0.ua: In the illustration I can see…
speaking.0.phrases.2.ua: In the background you can see…
speaking.0.tips.0: Go from the general to the details: **gdzie → kto → co robi → jak się czuje → co dalej**. These are exactly the four steps the examiner expects.
speaking.0.tips.1: Don't know a word — go around it: «taki stół do pracy» instead of «biurko». Silence is worse than a paraphrase.
speaking.0.tips.2: Guesses sound natural with **prawdopodobnie / chyba / wygląda na** — and they show range in your language.
speaking.1.promptUa: Talk about the job you would like to do in the future. Explain why this job interests you.
speaking.1.phrases.0.ua: My dream is to work as… (a profession)
speaking.1.phrases.3.ua: Right now I'm studying / working in order to…
speaking.1.tips.0: The construction «**marzę o** + locative» (marzę o pracy) is gender-neutral: you don't have to choose «-ł/-ła».
speaking.1.tips.1: **Żeby** + infinitive/past = «in order to»: it shows a more complex sentence already at B1.
speaking.1.tips.2: Finish with a conclusion («Myślę, że…»): the answer then sounds complete.
speaking.2.promptUa: You are phoning the shop «Smak-Pol» about a job advert for a shop assistant. You are talking to a company employee. Find out the details and arrange an interview.
speaking.2.phrases.0.ua: I'm calling about the job advert.
speaking.2.tips.0: Respond **exactly to the question**, then add one detail of your own — that makes a live conversation, not «yes/no».
speaking.2.tips.1: Didn't understand — ask again: «Przepraszam, czy mógłby Pan powtórzyć?» That isn't a minus, it's a skill.
speaking.2.tips.2: The conditional («wolałabym», «czy mogłabym») sounds polite — use it in requests.
writing.0.promptUa: Tomorrow you have an important meeting at work, but you are ill and can't come. Write a short message to a colleague: apologise, explain the reason and ask for help.
writing.0.phrases.1.ua: I've had a temperature since yesterday.
writing.0.tips.0: In a short text **every sentence = one point**. Three points — three sentences, plus a greeting/closing.
writing.0.tips.1: Forms of address in letters are capitalised: **Cię, Ci, Ty, Twój**.
writing.1.promptUa: You found an advert: the café «Pod Lipą» is looking for a part-time barista. Write to the owner: introduce yourself, describe your experience, explain why you want to work there, and ask about working hours and pay.
writing.1.phrases.1.ua: I am writing in response to the job advert…
writing.1.phrases.3.ua: I would like to ask about…
writing.1.tips.0: Letter structure: **salutation → purpose → about yourself → motivation → questions → closing**. Each block is a separate paragraph.
writing.1.tips.1: Formal: **Pan/Pani/Państwo** with a capital letter; no «cześć» and no «ty».
writing.1.tips.2: Write **ponieważ / dlatego / gdyż** — they count towards the «spójność» criterion.
listening.0.intro: Listen to the conversation twice and choose the correct answers.
grammar.0.intro: Choose the correct form. Pay attention to the cases after prepositions.
grammar.0.questions.0.why: After **jako** — nominative: «pracuję jako kierownik». In Ukrainian «працюю керівником» (instrumental) — here that is a mistake.
grammar.0.questions.3.why: A single action in the past — perfective: «poszłam». «Chodziłam» — repeated.
grammar.0.questions.4.why: After «jeśli» + future: «jeśli dostanę → przeprowadzę się». The conditional isn't needed here.
